editorial.headline: Government Construction Institutions: Closed to Foreign Registration
editorial.standfirst: This government-institution activity covers the guidance, development and administration of construction—and is closed to PMA nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 84145 concerns the work of government institutions in construction.** Its stated scope is the fostering, development and administration of the construction field, with government public-works institutions given as an example. The emphasis is therefore on the institutional public function described in the record: guiding, developing and organising construction activity through a government body.

The record does not identify any business scale as open to this activity. That absence matters. There is no listed opening for micro, small, medium or large-scale registration, so the activity should not be presented as available at a particular commercial scale on the basis of this record. The entity described is a government institution operating in the construction field, rather than an applicant whose eligibility can be inferred from a scale category.

Nationally, the position is unequivocal. The PMA status is **TERTUTUP**, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of **0%**. A foreign investor therefore cannot register this activity as a PMA activity or hold a foreign ownership stake within it under the national position recorded here. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021; the editorial conclusion is not a matter of commercial appetite or construction demand, but of the classification’s stated foreign-investment status.

Bali reaches the same practical result: the Bali status is **TERTUTUP**, and PMA registration is blocked. A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali under this record. There is, however, a precise qualification worth retaining. The Bali reason places the activity at medium-high or high risk and says it is not blocked by Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. That does not make the activity available: its recorded Bali status remains closed. The record also calls for verification by address, so any location-specific reading should be checked at the relevant address rather than assumed from the moratorium alone.
editorial.pullQuote: The fact that the activity sits outside Bali’s PMA moratorium does not make it available: its recorded Bali status remains closed.
